card.keepWhy: Goodbye, with drums, and a promise to come back.
sources: Ganesh Chaturthi, in the month of Bhadrapada, especially celebrated in Maharashtra; images of Ganesha welcomed at home or in public pandals for one and a half to ten days
Ganesh visarjan: immersion of the image in the sea, a river or a lake at the festival’s end
The chant “Ganpati Bappa Morya, pudhchya varshi lavkar ya” (Marathi: come early next year), the film’s note
Ganesha honored first: Shiva Purana (week two, “How Ganesha got his head”)
check: “Morya” is often linked to the saint Morya Gosavi of Chinchwad; the lesson doesn’t explain it. Confirm that’s fine.
Before immersion, families traditionally bid Ganesha’s presence farewell in a short rite (uttara puja); the lesson doesn’t mention it. Confirm acceptable.

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? is something good ending for you right now? a place, a season, a chapter.
options: then this festival is for you. listen.
then listen to how they say goodbye.
good. keep this one for when it does.

steps.line: Every year, for Ganesh Chaturthi, families bring home a statue of Ganesha.

steps.q: Ganesha’s own story begins with his mother shaping him with her hands. From what?
steps.why: Parvati shaped him from the paste on her skin (many tellings say turmeric) and gave him life. Many families still welcome a Ganesha shaped by hand from clay.

steps.line: They welcome him like a guest: they feed him sweets, and sing to him, for days.

steps.q: After days as an honored guest, what do you guess happens to Ganesha?
o: He stays in the home all year
He’s taken to the temple to stay
He’s carried to the water, and let go
steps.why: They let him go, with drums and dancing. Watch.

steps.line: Then, at the end of the festival, they carry him to the sea or a river, dancing and drumming.
steps.label: Ganesh visarjan

steps.line: And gently, they let him go into the water.
steps.label: Ganesh visarjan

steps.q: Many families say Ganesha takes something with him when he goes. What?
steps.why: He’s Vighnaharta, the remover of obstacles. Many believe he carries the family’s troubles away as he returns home to Shiva and Parvati.

steps.line: As he goes, crowds chant: Ganpati Bappa Morya! Come back soon next year!
steps.label: Ganpati Bappa Morya

steps.q: “Ganpati Bappa Morya!” Bappa is a loving word for father. Who was Morya?
o: The first town to hold it
steps.why: Many trace it to Morya Gosavi, a Ganesha devotee near Pune centuries ago. The crowd shouts a saint’s name along with the god he loved.

steps.line: Letting go makes room for the next beginning.
steps.label: today

steps.q: Ganesh Chaturthi was once mostly a home festival. Who brought it into the streets, in the 1890s?
steps.why: In 1893, Bal Gangadhar Tilak brought Ganesha into the streets of Pune, partly to gather people when British rule limited public meetings.

say: here’s what i love. the festival doesn’t pretend goodbye isn’t coming. it dances all the way to the water.
many hindus see visarjan as a lesson in letting go: welcome with love, release with love, and trust the return. he goes back to the water, and the welcome comes again next year.

steps.q: Families welcome Ganesha, then let him go, every single year. From the lesson, what does that teach about endings?
o: Nothing good lasts, so don’t hold on
An ending can make room for a return
steps.why: Every goodbye at the water leads to next year’s welcome. Letting go is how the next beginning starts.

today.say: let go of one thing this week that’s done its job: an old file, a shirt you’ve outgrown, a plan that’s finished. thank it, and let it go. many families sing a farewell aarti to ganesha. you can listen to one, join in, or just say thank you. it’s your choice.
options: then thank it, and let it go. bappa would.
it is. that’s why they bring drums. go gently.
